blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Singapore have concluded negotiations to update their nearly 50-year-old double taxation agreement to reflect changes in their economies and the international tax landscape. On Friday, the Department of Finance (DOF) announced that negotiators held discussions in Singapore from Sept. 22 to 25 for four days. READ: Oman, Singapore move to finalize tax treaties this year The renegotiation will update the agreement first signed by the two countries in 1977. “The Philippines is committed to strengthening tax cooperation across the region.
